text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Vietnam and India have set a target of a two-way annual; trade turnover worth at least $200 million by the turn of the century.
-- Greece could help Vietnam promote ties with the European Union and aid in Vietnam's bid to join the World Trade Organisation.
-- Party members and their spouses and children are prohibited from engaging in private business, according to a regulation set by the Ho Chi Minh City Party Unit.
-- The last king of the Vietnamese Nguyen dynasty, Bao Dai died last Friday in Paris. He was 83.
-- The cabinet has discussed draft banking laws.
-- Vice President Nguyen Thi Binh says Vietnamese citizens should rely on theirselves and not on the state.
-- Vietnam has invested more than one trillion dong ($85.58 million) to upgrade and repair road systems in the Mekong River Delta.
-- Vietnam's telecom industry is hoping to meet a target of six telephones per 100 people by the year 2000. At present, that ratio is 1.89 per 100 people.
-- Through 1,366 inspections in the first half of 1997, the State Inspectorate has found more than 5,000 units and individuals who have violated laws and state policies.
-- Israeli Vice Prime Minister Rafael Eitan starts his four-day visit to Vietnam on Monday to discuss measures to enhance co-operation in rural, agricultural and environmental issues.

-- Communist Party General Secretary Do Muoi, visiting the Toyota Car Joint-venture on Sunday, has affirmed Vietnam's open-door policy regarding foreign investors, underlining the co-operation principle of equality, mutual repect and benefit.
